en: Out of kindness to me you have spoken the supreme secret, the knowledge of the Self, and by your words my delusion is gone.
speaker: Arjuna said

sa: भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया।
tr: bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśo mayā
en: I have heard from you in detail how beings come into existence and pass away, lotus-eyed one, and of your imperishable greatness.
It is just as you have described yourself, supreme Lord. Yet I long to see your divine form, Supreme Person.

sa: मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो।
tr: manyase yadi tacchakyaṃ mayā draṣṭumiti prabho
en: If you think I am able to see it, Lord, master of yoga, then show me your imperishable Self.

sa: पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
tr: paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ
en: Behold, Partha, my forms by the hundreds and the thousands: many kinds, divine, of many colours and shapes.
speaker: Krishna said

en: Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the twin Ashvins and the Maruts; behold many wonders never seen before, Bharata.
Behold here today, Gudakesha, the whole universe, moving and unmoving, gathered in one place within my body, and whatever else you wish to see.

sa: न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा।
दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ॥
tr: na tu māṃ śakyase draṣṭumanenaiva svacakṣuṣā
divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogamaiśvaram
en: But you cannot see me with these eyes of yours. I give you divine sight: behold my sovereign yoga.
Having spoken thus, O king, Hari, the great lord of yoga, showed Partha his supreme, sovereign form,
speaker: Sanjaya said

en: with countless mouths and eyes, countless wondrous sights, countless divine ornaments and countless raised divine weapons,
wearing divine garlands and robes, anointed with divine fragrances, all-wondrous, radiant, infinite, facing every direction.

sa: यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
tr: yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ
en: If the light of a thousand suns were to blaze forth at once in the sky, it might resemble the splendour of that great Self.
There, in the body of the God of gods, Pandava then saw the whole universe, divided in many ways, gathered as one.
Then Dhananjaya, overwhelmed with wonder, his hair standing on end, bowed his head to the Lord and spoke with joined palms.
I see in your body, O God, all the gods and the hosts of beings: Brahma the lord seated on the lotus, all the sages and the divine serpents.
speaker: Arjuna said

en: I see you with countless arms, bellies, mouths and eyes, infinite in form on every side. I see no end, no middle and no beginning of you, Lord of the universe, universal form.
I see you with crown, mace and discus, a mass of radiance shining everywhere, hard to look at, blazing all round like fire and sun, immeasurable.
You are the imperishable, the supreme one to be known; you are the final resting place of this universe; you are the undying guardian of eternal dharma; you are, I believe, the eternal Person.
Without beginning, middle or end, of infinite power, with countless arms, the sun and moon your eyes, I see you, your mouth a blazing fire, burning this universe with your radiance.
The space between heaven and earth and all the directions are filled by you alone. Seeing this wondrous, terrible form of yours, great Self, the three worlds tremble.
These hosts of gods enter into you; some, afraid, praise you with joined palms. Bands of great sages and the perfected cry "Peace!" and praise you with abundant hymns.
The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, the Ashvins, the Maruts and the ancestors, and hosts of celestial musicians, yakshas, demons and the perfected all gaze at you in amazement.
Seeing your great form, mighty-armed, with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs and feet, many bellies and terrible tusks, the worlds tremble, and so do I.

sa: धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो ॥
tr: dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi śamaṃ ca viṣṇo
en: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing in many colours, mouths gaping, huge eyes burning, my inmost self trembles, Vishnu, and I find no courage and no peace.

sa: दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म
tr: diśo na jāne na labhe ca śarma
en: Seeing your mouths with their terrible tusks, like the fires at the end of time, I lose all sense of direction and find no refuge. Be gracious, Lord of gods, refuge of the world.
All these sons of Dhritarashtra, with the hosts of kings, Bhishma, Drona and Karna, together with the chief warriors on our side too,
rush headlong into your fearful mouths with their terrible tusks; some are seen caught between your teeth, their heads crushed to powder.
As the many torrents of rivers race toward the ocean, so these heroes of the world of men enter your flaming mouths.
As moths rush into a blazing flame to their destruction, so these worlds rush into your mouths to their destruction.
Devouring all the worlds on every side with your flaming mouths, you lick your lips; your fierce rays fill the whole universe with radiance and scorch it, Vishnu.
Tell me who you are, with this terrible form. I bow to you, best of gods; be gracious. I wish to know you, the primal one, for I do not understand what you are doing.
I am Time, the mighty destroyer of worlds, here engaged in destroying the worlds. Even without you, none of these warriors arrayed in the opposing armies will survive.
speaker: Krishna said

en: So stand up and win glory. Conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. They have already been slain by me; be merely the instrument, you who can shoot with either hand.

sa: द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च
tr: droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca jayadrathaṃ ca
en: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna and the other heroic warriors are already slain by me; kill them, do not waver. Fight, and you will conquer your rivals in battle.
Hearing these words of Keshava, the crowned one, trembling, joined his palms and bowed; and bowing again, overcome with fear, he spoke to Krishna in a choked voice.
speaker: Sanjaya said

en: It is right, Hrishikesha, that the world delights and rejoices in praising you; demons flee in fear in every direction, and all the hosts of the perfected bow down.
speaker: Arjuna said

en: And why should they not bow to you, great Self, greater even than Brahma, the first creator? Infinite Lord of gods, refuge of the world, you are the imperishable, being and non-being, and what lies beyond both.

sa: वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम
tr: vettāsi vedyaṃ ca paraṃ ca dhāma
en: You are the first God, the ancient Person, the supreme resting place of this universe; you are the knower and what is to be known, the highest abode. By you the universe is pervaded, infinite form.
You are Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati and the great-grandsire. Salutations to you, a thousand times salutations, and again and again salutations to you!
Salutations to you in front and behind, salutations on every side, you who are all. Infinite in power, immeasurable in might, you pervade all, and so you are all.

sa: हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति।
tr: he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti
en: Thinking of you only as a friend, I rashly called you "Krishna! Yadava! Friend!", not knowing your greatness, out of carelessness or affection;
and if in jest I showed you disrespect, while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in company, Achyuta, I ask forgiveness of you, the immeasurable.

You are the father of this world, of all that moves and does not move; you are its worshipful and most honoured teacher. There is none equal to you in the three worlds; how could there be any greater, you of incomparable power?
So, bowing and laying my body down before you, I seek your grace, adorable Lord. As a father with his son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved, please bear with me, O God.
I rejoice to have seen what was never seen before, yet my mind is shaken with fear. Show me, God, that other form of yours; be gracious, Lord of gods, refuge of the world.
I wish to see you as before, with crown, mace and discus in hand. Take that four-armed form, thousand-armed one, universal form.
By my grace, Arjuna, through my own yoga, I have shown you this supreme form, radiant, universal, infinite and primal, which no one but you has ever seen.
speaker: Krishna said

en: Not by the Vedas, nor by sacrifices, nor by study, nor by gifts, nor by rituals, nor by fierce austerities can I be seen in this form in the world of men by anyone but you, great hero of the Kurus.

sa: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो
tr: mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍhabhāvo
en: Do not be afraid or bewildered at seeing this terrible form of mine. Free from fear and glad at heart, behold once more that form of mine.
Having spoken thus to Arjuna, Vasudeva showed his own form again; and taking on his gentle form once more, the great-souled one comforted the frightened Arjuna.
speaker: Sanjaya said

en: Seeing this gentle human form of yours, Janardana, I am composed again, and my mind is restored to its natural state.
speaker: Arjuna said

en: This form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see. Even the gods always long to see it.
speaker: Krishna said

sa: नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया।
शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा ॥
tr: nāhaṃ vedairna tapasā na dānena na cejyayā
śakya evaṃvidho draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavānasi māṃ yathā
en: Not by the Vedas, nor by austerity, nor by gifts, nor by sacrifice can I be seen as you have seen me.

sa: ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ॥
tr: jñātuṃ dṛṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca paraṃtapa
en: But by undivided devotion, Arjuna, I can be known in this way, seen as I truly am, and entered into, scorcher of foes.

sa: निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥
tr: nirvairaḥ sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ sa māmeti pāṇḍava
en: Whoever works for me, makes me the goal, is devoted to me, free from attachment and without enmity toward any being, comes to me, Pandava.
